reviewer: Claude agent review (Fable 5.1), not a human historian
text: 2026-10-11: fifth approval, text only, after one round of three blockers. The owner asked for the scene prose to be rewritten as pure storytelling (README step 4): events happen on the page in order and with confidence; inside a scene no 'the poet says', 'the stone does not say', 'historians think', 'disputed', 'perhaps' and no scholar names; where the record is silent the storyteller chooses one plausible telling and discloses that choice in the scene's dramatised list, which the evidence page shows beside facts.json. The twelve scenes' paragraphs and dramatised lists, the introduction and the summary were rewritten; three scenes gained fact ids (scene-03 f-vikramaditya-recovery, scene-10 f-harsha-xuanzang, scene-11 f-vatapi-543). facts.json and the thirteen pictures are unchanged from the fourth approval; the illustration notes and imageSha256 below are carried over unchanged.

Read the whole story.json (introduction, twelve scenes with paragraphs, dramatised lists and facts[], summary, teaser, subtitle, didYouKnow, visitToday, provenance, illustration disclosure, content note) against facts.json, research/badami-chalukya.md (including Appendix B, Beal ii 255-257) and research/badami-chalukya-verified.md (Kielhorn's verbatim vv. 11-37 with footnotes, the Kuram plates with the Sanskrit, the Badami Mahamalla rock, Beal i 213-215 on Harsha, Tabari in Nöldeke p. 371). Every verse the scenes draw on was compared line by line: 11-13 (scene 2), 14-16 (scenes 2-3), 17-19 (scene 4), 20-21 (scene 5), 22 (scene 6), 23-24 with fn. 6 on Agastya (scene 7), 25-28 with fn. 7 on the three saktis (scene 8), 29-32 with fn. 4, 6 and 7 (scene 9), 33-37 (scene 10); Beal i 213 (the vow, 5,000 elephants, cavalry left as ಸಾವಿರಾರು, 50,000 foot, six years, 60,000 and 100,000); Beal ii 255-257 (the people, woman's clothes, the champions, the drunk elephants, Pu-lo-ki-she, 'not yet conquered their troops'); Kuram (Pariyala, Manimangala, Suramara 'etc.', vijaya on the back, Vatapi churned like Agastya's demon); the Badami rock (nine lines, Mahamalla, thirteenth year, Vatapi, name lost); Tabari (36th year, envoys, letters, elephant, sword, white falcon, brocade); Fleet (Chitrakantha, three kings, Kanchi, Gadval 674 at Uragapura, Adityavarman, Vijayabhattarika, Lokesvara for three conquests of Kanchi). No name, number, year, relationship or sequence inside a scene contradicts them.

The storytelling rule was checked mechanically and by reading: a scripted scan of every paragraph of the introduction, the scenes and the summary finds none of ಕವಿ ಹೇಳುತ್ತಾನೆ, ಕಲ್ಲು ಹೇಳುವುದಿಲ್ಲ, ಇತಿಹಾಸಕಾರರು, ಕೀಲ್‌ಹಾರ್ನ್, ವಿವಾದಿತ, ದಾಖಲೆ, ಶಾಸನ, ಬಹುಶಃ, ಊಹೆ, ಫ್ಲೀಟ್, ದೀಕ್ಷಿತ್ or ಗೊತ್ತಿಲ್ಲ; Ravikirti cutting his verses (scene 10) and 'ಅವನ ಕವಿ ಅವನ ಬಗ್ಗೆ ಬರೆದ ಕೊನೆಯ ಪದ: ಆಳುತ್ತಿದ್ದಾನೆ' (scene 11) are narrative, not commentary. Years appear in prose only where the records are dated or hedged with ಸುಮಾರು (543, 578, c. 610, 634, c. 641 as 'a few years later', c. 642, 674); the Harsha war has no year in prose and the three candidate years are in scene 7's note.

Inventions and inferences told as fact, each disclosed in its own scene's dramatised list: the ten-year-old at Cave III, the conch, the lamps, the cave 'still new' at a father's death whose year is unrecorded (scene 1); the palace watching him, the yuvaraja whisper as Kielhorn's conjecture, the two companions and the night stair (scene 2); the exile at the Ganga court of Talakad, Durvinita opening the door, the marriage during those years, the Alupas' early help, the envoys, the last battle, the coronation, his age, 610 as an estimate (scene 3); Govinda's night envoy and gift, 'ಬನವಾಸಿ ಬಾಗಿಲು ತೆರೆಯಿತು', 'a few years' (scene 4); the Konkan, the months of shipbuilding, the dawn, Puri's disputed site, the Ajanta ship (scene 5); the three kings' deliberation and their coming to Vatapi, the pilgrim's figures (scene 6); the Narmada as historians' inference, dusk, fires, the dawn crossing, the day-long battle, the reddened river, 'ಹಿಂದಕ್ಕೆ ಹೋದ, ಮತ್ತೆ ದಕ್ಷಿಣಕ್ಕೆ ಬರಲಿಲ್ಲ', Xuanzang's months at Harsha's court (scene 7); the three saktis tied to the exile, 'before the army came', five centuries of Eastern Chalukyas (scene 8); the Mayurasharma memory, the Pallava caves, Mahendravarma named as historians' identification, his pride, the monsoon (scene 9); the pilgrim's look, no meeting with the king, the drunk-elephant link to the Narmada, the Persian embassy told as true with Nöldeke's reading and its doubters named (scene 10); Narasimhavarman's revenge, the army, the retreats, the ageing king, the Malaprabha, the smoke, the three possible deaths, thirty years, his parentage as historians' identification (scene 11); the scattered sons, the journey to the Gangas, thirteen years as Dikshit's estimate (scene 12). The introduction now says that large events, most names and the years are from the stone and that one plausible path is the storyteller's where the stone is silent, and sends the reader to the last pages.

Blockers found on the first read of the rewrite and fixed before this approval: scene 7 said Harsha had conquered 'ten kings', a number in no source, now 'ಎಷ್ಟೋ ರಾಜರು ಬಿದ್ದಿದ್ದರು'; scene 7's note disclosed 'ಹಿಂದಕ್ಕೆ ಹೋದ' but not 'ಮತ್ತೆ ದಕ್ಷಿಣಕ್ಕೆ ಬರಲಿಲ್ಲ', now both, with the note that the pilgrim says only 'not yet conquered'; scene 11 narrated the Pallava mason cutting his record behind the Mallikarjuna temple in 642, a temple of the 11th-12th century, now a rock on the lake's north shore with the temple named only as today's locator. Nits fixed on the same pass: the introduction's claim that 'events, names and years are from the stone' softened; Talakad, the exile marriage and the Alupas added to scene 3's note; Kirtivarman's unrecorded death year added to scene 1's note; 'ಹೊಸ ಸೇವೆಗೆ' trimmed to the verse's 'services rendered'; the Gurjaras no longer placed in Gujarat; 'strove to conquer the Cholas' restored before the prosperity of v. 31, and the summary says ಸಮೃದ್ಧಿ ತಂದು instead of 'made allies'; the sixfold army trimmed to Kielhorn's 'hereditary troops and the rest'; Xuanzang's visit 'ಕೆಲವು ವರ್ಷಗಳ ನಂತರ' instead of 'around the same time'; the thirteen-year occupation and Narasimhavarman's parentage disclosed in the scene notes that use them; 'ಈವರೆಗಿನ ಕಥೆ' in scene 10. Open for the next facts.json pass only: f-persian-letter's disputed note still describes the story's earlier hedged telling of Tabari; the hedge now lives in scene 10's dramatised note.

Kannada: natural told-story register with the book's refrains (the rock stair, lord of three seas) carrying through; names consistent (ಪುಲಿಕೇಶಿ, ಮಂಗಳೇಶ, ಕೀರ್ತಿವರ್ಮ, ದುರ್ವಿನೀತ, ಹರ್ಷ, ಹ್ಯುಯೆನ್ ತ್ಸಾಂಗ್, ರವಿಕೀರ್ತಿ, ಮಹೇಂದ್ರವರ್ಮ, ನರಸಿಂಹವರ್ಮ, ಕುಬ್ಜ ವಿಷ್ಣುವರ್ಧನ, ವಿಕ್ರಮಾದಿತ್ಯ); no em dashes; NFC; adults' tone; the woman's-clothes custom and the reddened lake are the sources' words and the content note covers them. story.facts is byte-identical to facts.json (41 facts); every scene facts[] and didYouKnow id resolves and each scene's facts cover its claims; the summary agrees with the scenes. storySha256 above is the sha256 of story.json as approved; imageSha256 is unchanged because no picture changed.
illustrations: All thirteen WebPs (cover, scene-01 to scene-12) were opened and compared with their scene paragraphs, alt texts and bible/style.md; forts, letters, horses' feet, ships and far banks were inspected in enlarged crops. scene-09 and scene-11 are the regenerated versions (22:26 and 22:29) and were reopened after regeneration.

Blockers fixed before approval: scene-11 had modern Kannada-shaped glyphs on the Pallava-Grantha rock, now only chalk guide-lines and chisel scratches; scene-09 had a tiered Dravida temple on a Badami-type cliff on the Kaveri's far bank, now coconut groves and thatched huts only; scene-05's single-masted ships contradicted an alt text and a fact that promised three masts, now disclosed in the alt, in f-ships-visual and in the scene's dramatised note.

cover: Pulikeshi as king with tall jewelled kirita, pearls, armlets, patterned dhoti and sash, barefoot, straight double-edged sword, standard-bearer with the boar banner (boar with sun and moon); Badami's two red horns, caves, lake and brick-timber town behind. Nits: cruciform European-looking crossguard; the north-hill citadel drawn as a masonry castle with square towers (no loopholes, battlements or cannon).

scene-01: Cave III verandah with square bracketed pillars, Vishnu on Sesha in relief, boar-emblem hanging; the boy bare-chested in white dhoti with a small gold necklace and no crown; the lake and the red fort hill opposite. Same castle nit on the hill.

scene-02: night, the prince in ochre dhoti with sacred thread, earrings, short beard and a straight sword at the hip, no crown, with two companions and a torch on a rock stair between boulders; lamps on the lake. The citadel above is lit as a tower-castle (nit); the group reads as climbing rather than descending (alt says descending).

scene-03: dawn coronation on the lake shore, kirita crown, white umbrella, boar banners, elephants, conch blowers, round shields, straight sword, oil lamps; caves in the cliff behind, bare-rock hill with steps. Clean.

scene-04: Pulikeshi on an elephant under a white umbrella with the boar banner above a moated brick Banavasi on the Varada with water birds and a vast camp. Nits: crenellated walls and timber siege towers (unsourced), a tall vimana inside the city; soldiers in red cloth head-wraps.

scene-05: dawn mist, laterite headland fort with plain walls and thatched buildings (no cannon, no loopholes), hundreds of high-stemmed ships with painted eyes, oars and awnings, square sails, boar banner and the king on the lead ship; no lateen, stern rudder, outrigger or European hull. Single masts disclosed (see above).

scene-06: Harsha with top-knot and jewelled band, white and gold Gupta-style dhoti and shawl, pearl strings, on an elephant under a white umbrella; plain white banners and umbrellas, thousands of elephants, cavalry and spearmen in white head-wraps, distant river and temple spires. Nit: a possible stirrup on the white horse at far left, ambiguous at this resolution; no boar banner on Harsha's side.

scene-07: dusk on a wide sandy river, Pulikeshi in kirita on an elephant with boar banners, spears and round shields; Harsha's host across the water under dark plain banners and golden umbrellas, forested hills behind. Clean.
scene-08: Kolleru at sunset, red water, elephants with boar cloths and banners, soldiers with round shields, wreckage and fallen figures only at a distance, water birds. Clean, no close-up gore.

scene-09 (regenerated): a long line of war elephants wading a river in spate under boar banners, soldiers with spears on their backs, coconut groves, huts and small boats on the far bank; no buildings of any period. Clean.

scene-10: flat-roofed sandstone Meguti temple on a hill above the Malaprabha village; the shaven Ravikirti in white dhoti and uttariya with a palm leaf; a mason on a bamboo scaffold cutting letters. Nits: the letters are AI pseudo-script (Brahmi-like, not modern Kannada); a tall shikhara in the village below.

scene-11 (regenerated): a Pallava mason with mallet and chisel over chalk guide-lines on a boulder at the lake edge, no letters; two guards in white head-wraps with spears and round shields; the four caves, the town with smoke, the citadel on the north hill. Nit: the citadel is again a tower-castle.

scene-12: Vikramaditya in kirita on a grey horse with cloth saddle and bare foot (no stirrup), straight sword raised, boar banners and elephants behind, townspeople with flowers, caves and lake. Nit: tower-castle on the hill.

No image shows a helmet, mail, a curved sword, a lion or gandabherunda emblem, a gopuram, a cannon, a loopholed battlement, modern script on stone, or a Vijayanagara or Mughal crown; the boar banner appears only on the Chalukya side; the young prince is uncrowned in scene-02 and crowned from scene-03; Harsha wears Gupta-style dress with plain banners.
limitations: This is an AI review by a Claude agent; no human historian or epigraphist has read the text or checked the images.

Fact checking was limited to the research files in data/history-src/research (Kielhorn's EI VI translation as transcribed on whatisindia.com, Beal 1884 from archive.org OCR, Hultzsch SII I, SII XI no. 1 via DHARMA, Nöldeke 1879 OCR, Fleet 1896) and did not re-fetch the primary sources; the Bijapur-Mumbai plates (2017) were not read at first hand by anyone on this project.

The Ganga parentage of Vikramaditya I and Durvinita's help, the thirteen-year Pallava occupation, the identification of the v. 29 Pallava as Mahendravarman I and of Narasimhavarman I as his son, and the five centuries of the Eastern Chalukyas rest on Dikshit 1980, Sastri 1960 and Fleet 1896 as reported in the research, not on a primary text read here.

No portrait of any Badami Chalukya king survives; Pulikeshi's face, every setting and the 7th-century buildings of the Badami citadel are invented, as the disclosure and f-badami-fort-visual say. The citadel is drawn as a masonry tower-castle in five images; the bible asked for a bare-rock citadel, and the fact text was softened to cover this rather than regenerating.
The ships in scene-05 are single-masted, simplified from the three-masted Ajanta model; the scene's alt, f-ships-visual and the dramatised note disclose this.

The engraved letters in scene-10 are AI pseudo-script that only resembles early Brahmi; they are not readable text and must not be taken as a rendering of the Aihole inscription. scene-11 shows no letters at all.
The images were judged at 1600x900 WebP; small background details (crowd dress, distant buildings in scenes 4, 6 and 10, the possible stirrup in scene 6) could not be verified individually.
